subject.title: GitHub OAuth consent screen uses personal ClawdHub app branding

question: Should production GitHub sign-in be moved to an official OpenClaw-owned OAuth App now, and who should perform the GitHub OAuth App plus Convex production secret rotation?
rationale: The source tree shows the auth path and required env variables, but the actual consent branding, client ownership, callback URL, and production secret values are outside the repository and affect the auth trust boundary.

options.title: Rotate to official OAuth App
options.body: Create or transfer the OAuth App under official OpenClaw ownership, update Convex production AUTH_GITHUB_ID and AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET, then verify web and CLI auth before closing.

options.title: Document a temporary exception
options.body: If the personal app is intentionally retained for now, record the owner, callback URL, and migration plan in operator docs/specs so reviewers know the risk is accepted.

options.title: Defer as tracked ops work
options.body: Keep this issue open but move it to a named release or ops checklist so the auth trust concern is not lost.

recommendation.title: Rotate to official OAuth App
recommendation.body: Create or transfer the OAuth App under official OpenClaw ownership, update Convex production AUTH_GITHUB_ID and AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET, then verify web and CLI auth before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS routes the auth and deploy security surfaces to this team, and the remaining decision is production auth-provider ownership plus secret rotation.
